import smtplib
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email.mime.base import MIMEBase
from email import encoders

msg = MIMEMultipart()
msg["From"] = "agent@cuga.dev"
msg["To"] = "bob@example.com"
msg["Subject"] = "Customer Activity Report - Maya Chen"

body = """Hi Bob,

Please find attached the Customer Activity Report for Maya Chen.

The report covers the following orders:
- ORD-6C71B1
- ORD-5B048F

Best regards,
Cuga Agent"""

msg.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

with open("docs/customer_report.pdf", "rb") as f:
    part = MIMEBase("application", "octet-stream")
    part.set_payload(f.read())
    encoders.encode_base64(part)
    part.add_header("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=customer_report.pdf")
    msg.attach(part)

try:
    server = smtplib.SMTP("localhost", 25)
    server.sendmail("agent@cuga.dev", "bob@example.com", msg.as_string())
    server.quit()
    print("Email sent successfully to bob@example.com")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"SMTP localhost failed: {e}")
    try:
        server = smtplib.SMTP("mailhog", 1025)
        server.sendmail("agent@cuga.dev", "bob@example.com", msg.as_string())
        server.quit()
        print("Email sent successfully via mailhog to bob@example.com")
    except Exception as e2:
        print(f"Mailhog also failed: {e2}")
        # Save the email as .eml file as fallback
        with open("docs/customer_report_email.eml", "w") as ef:
            ef.write(msg.as_string())
        print("Email saved as docs/customer_report_email.eml as fallback")
'''
